analysis.title: The $320 Billion Question: Wall Street Split On Whether Warsh's Fed Will Keep Funding Bessent's Bill Binge
key_insights: JPMorgan's 2027 Treasury supply outlook ('One cannot live on T-bills alone') expects Treasury to start raising coupon auction sizes in August 2027 because traditional bill buyers are 'no longer keeping pace with the pace of issuance'.
Goldman moved its call for larger 2Y-to-10Y auctions from May to August after the November refunding, so the two banks now agree on the start date for coupon increases.
The two banks are roughly $320 billion apart on who absorbs net bill supply in 2027. The gap comes down to the Fed's bill purchases.

JPMorgan assumes the Fed buys about $180BN of bills in 2027, all from reinvesting MBS paydowns at roughly $15BN a month, down from $360BN in 2026, with no reserve management purchases. Goldman has reserve management purchases restarting at $10BN a month this month and rising to about $25BN a month from Q2 2027, on top of MBS reinvestment.

JPMorgan has private investors absorbing $1.011 trillion of net new bills in 2027 versus $538BN in 2026. Bills go from under a third of the public's net take to about half. With the debt ceiling implying negative net bill supply in 1H27, most of that likely lands in 2H27.

The federal deficit widened by $217BN to $1.992 trillion in FY26. JPMorgan forecasts $2.06 trillion (6.1% of GDP) in FY27 and $2.25 trillion in FY28, assuming the average effective tariff rate rises to 13.8% from 11.2%. Court challenges or a changed Congress could undermine that assumption.

At current auction sizes JPMorgan estimates a cumulative funding gap of about $1.6 trillion over FY27-28. Separately, the median primary dealer saw a $2.14 trillion shortfall in FY28-29, per Treasury's debt managers speaking to the TBAC.

The bill share of marketable debt rose from about 15% at end-2022 to just under 23% now. JPMorgan expects it above 24% by end-2027 even with coupon increases. Treasury's own do-nothing scenario has it near 28% by 2029.

Three-month bills now trade cheap to SOFR for the first time since late 2022 despite an ample funding environment, while 2Y notes richened on an asset swap basis YTD. JPMorgan reads this as early signs that bill demand is becoming somewhat inelastic.

JPMorgan sees money-fund AUM growth slowing to mid-single digits, foreign official holdings providing less support, and stablecoin AUM stagnant for 18 months. Foreign official accounts sold $90 billion of Treasuries in the first weeks of the Iran war.

JPMorgan expects the debt limit to bind around February 2027, with Treasury about $694BN below it as of Nov 12. Net bill issuance turns negative through at least Q2 2027, and coupon increases start at the August refunding after the TGA rebuild.

JPMorgan's coupon path raises the 2Y and 5Y by $2BN a month from August and the 3Y by $1BN, with smaller increases in the 7Y and 10Y. Monthly coupon issuance reaches $406BN by December 2027 versus $366BN in January. Gross coupon, TIPS and FRN issuance totals $4.511 trillion in 2027, $116BN above 2026.

JPMorgan keeps the 20Y at $168BN and the 30Y at $276BN in 2027, rejecting Citi's call for long-end cuts. It cites solid long-end auction demand and good market functioning, and sees a risk that 20s and 30s get increased. Goldman's baseline is unchanged long-end sizes with risk skewed to a modest reduction.

Goldman has net coupon supply to the public falling to about $1.1 trillion in 2027 from $1.2 trillion in 2026, citing bill reliance, bigger buybacks and heavier redemptions. Weighted average maturity is projected to fall from 69 months to 68 by end-2027 and 67 by end-2028 on JPMorgan's numbers.

The New York Fed's schedule for Nov 16 to Dec 11 shows about $14BN of reinvestment purchases and no reserve management purchases, extending a pause that began in mid-August into a fourth month. The article reads this as supporting JPMorgan's Fed assumption over Goldman's.

JPMorgan sees a growing chance that Treasury introduces a 1-year SOFR-linked floating rate note in 2027, with several dealers and the TBAC discussing it at this month's refunding. It would not expect the 2-year T-bill FRN to be discontinued, but its size could shrink.

Rate-cost sensitivity cited by the article: each 25bps of Fed hiking adds roughly $17BN a year to interest on the existing bill stock, which grows by about $1 trillion a year. A December hike is described as fully priced after a hot CPI print last week.

The author (Zero Hedge) says JPMorgan is right on the math and Goldman is probably right on the outcome. The author expects the Fed to end up buying around half a trillion of bills in 2027 after a plumbing stress event following the debt ceiling resolution. This is the author's opinion, not a bank forecast.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Deficit widened in a year when nominal GDP grew more than 5.5%. Receipts rose 3% and outlays rose 6%, partly from tariff refunds after the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs.
Assumes tariff revenue recovers as the average effective tariff rate rises to 13.8% from 11.2%. A shortfall in tariff revenue would enlarge the deficit and bring forward coupon increases.
Continued widening implies sustained heavy Treasury issuance.

crypto_views: Stablecoin AUM has been stagnant for the last 18 months, per JPMorgan. Stablecoins were widely expected to be a growing buyer of Treasury bills and have not become one.
risk_factors: Tariff revenue fails to recover through court challenges or Congress, widening the deficit and bringing coupon increases forward.
Bill demand from money funds, foreign official accounts and stablecoins is not growing, while private absorption of bills nearly doubles in 2027.
Debt ceiling resolution forces a TGA rebuild and a surge in bill issuance in 2H27, coinciding with the first coupon increases.
Warsh's balance sheet task force could end MBS reinvestment into bills, lowering Fed purchases below JPMorgan's forecast in 2H27.
Treasury could cut long-end auction sizes or change the maturity mix unpredictably, a risk JPMorgan leaves open given the Treasury Secretary's focus on lower long-term rates.
Author's view: something in the market plumbing could snap once bills flood a market where they already trade cheap to SOFR.
vol_and_positioning: Three-month bills trade cheap to SOFR for the first time since late 2022, while 2Y notes have richened on an asset swap basis YTD.
A December Fed hike is described as fully priced after last week's hot CPI print.
Potential Fed balance sheet shrinkage under Chair Warsh's task force is flagged as a risk to bill demand in 2H27.
geopolitical: Foreign official accounts sold $90 billion of Treasuries in the first weeks of the Iran war, and are providing less support for bill demand.
The Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs, leading to tariff refunds. Pending Section 301 and 232 actions are expected to restore tariff revenue.
A Congress that just changed hands and more court challenges could interfere with the tariff revenue assumption.
cross_bank_references: Goldman moved its call for larger 2Y-to-10Y auctions from May to August, matching JPMorgan's August 2027 start.
JPMorgan keeps the 20Y at $168BN and the 30Y at $276BN, contrary to Citi's Jason Williams predicting cuts to 20Y and 30Y auctions.
Goldman's baseline is unchanged long-end sizes with risk skewed toward a modest reduction, somewhere between JPMorgan and Citi.
JPMorgan and Goldman are roughly $320 billion apart on the Fed's role in absorbing 2027 bill supply.
A BofA figure on bill-stock interest cost is cited as the basis for the author's napkin math.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects reserve management purchases of $10BN a month rising to about $25BN a month from Q2 2027, so the Fed absorbs roughly half a trillion of bills and private investors take only about $600BN.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan expects only MBS reinvestment of about $15BN a month, with Fed purchases of about $180BN, so private investors must absorb about $1.011 trillion of bills. Risks are skewed lower in 2H27 if Warsh's balance sheet task force ends MBS reinvestment.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The NY Fed schedule for Nov 16 to Dec 11 shows no reserve management purchases, extending the pause into a fourth month, which contradicts Goldman's expected restart this month.

tension_points.bull_case: Citi's Jason Williams expects Treasury to cut 20Y and 30Y auction sizes, possibly eliminating the 20Y.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan sees little rationale to cut an existing source of borrowing capacity when financing needs are rising, and cites solid long-end auction demand and good market functioning. It sees a risk that 20s and 30s are increased.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No cut came at the Nov 4 refunding. JPMorgan's 2027 table keeps the 20Y at $168BN and the 30Y at $276BN.

tension_points.bull_case: Treasury says at every refunding that demand for bills is strong and broad, citing growing private-sector demand and SOMA purchases.
tension_points.bear_case: JPMorgan sees early signs of inelastic bill demand. Bills trade cheap to SOFR for the first time since late 2022, money fund growth is slowing, foreign official support is lower and stablecoin AUM is flat. Goldman also flags risks of more price-sensitive bill absorption.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Bills richening back to or through SOFR, or private investors absorbing about $1 trillion of bills in 2H27 without further cheapening, would weaken the bear case.
